10 paired blocks; 4 chains/block; 1000 warmup + 10000 retained draws/chain.
Target: U=y^2/18+(5/2)*y+exp(-y)*sum(x_i^2)/2; beta=1; base mass I6; y~N(0,9), x_i|y~N(0,exp(y)).
Observables: all six coordinates and all 21 unique quadratic products; 27 total.
Original multi-chain Geyer initial-positive then initial-monotone sequence; biased autocovariance denominator N, no floor or hand-set lag cutoff.
Maximum of rank-normalized split and folded rank-normalized split R-hat; descriptive, no threshold.
Actual new physical-target gradients during retention only. NUTS counts every executed leapfrog leaf, including discarded/divergent/nonfinite leaves; excludes initial epsilon search, warmup and cached reuse. THC complete proposals cost L (scalar 10, periodic 5, conditional 30); aborted proposals can cost less. Thermostat-only operations are excluded. Not wall-clock cost.
E_b=1/(actual retained gradients per draw * worst physical-observable IAT); S is the geometric mean of ALL ten block efficiencies. Undefined blocks are never dropped or replaced.
Numerical-event rules (unchanged from each completed tuner; not identical counters):
NUTS: Original expanded funnel rule: any nonfinite leaf during warmup or retention, nonfinite selected sample, undefined required IAT or invalid gradient denominator makes the full score undefined. Finite divergences and depth hits are diagnostic, not separate score gates. Invalid leaves cannot be selected; do not force whole-transition rejection when a valid candidate exists.
THC: Original expanded funnel rule: any nonfinite trajectory during warmup or retention, undefined required IAT or invalid gradient denominator makes the full score undefined. A rejected proposal retains the previous q and s. Descriptive IAT/R-hat remain reported when estimable.
NUTS adaptation statistic is NOT a Metropolis acceptance probability and is reported separately from THC acceptance.
Same seed identifiers, physical starts and lengths in corresponding blocks. NUTS preserves its Numba thread-local legacy NumPy RNG; THC preserves its SeedSequence child streams. Random draws are NOT claimed to match between NUTS and THC. The three THC methods share the same raw child streams. Pairing hashes seal seeds, starts and lengths.
No final-data parameter selection. NUTS adapts only within the discarded warmup of each chain.
All three THC coordinates s persist. Only physical and thermostat momenta refresh; rejection restores q and s. Scalar and Periodic initial s=(-1,1,1,-1); Conditional initial s=(-6,-1,1,6).

h(s)=1+0.75*cos(s/0.25-pi/2); rho(s)=N(0,1); Q=128. Scalar periodic coupling, not target-informed geometry.
